plain: Create an isolated Python environment in a .venv folder so this project's packages don't leak into the system.
when: The first thing to run in any new Python project. Keeps dependencies reproducible and avoids 'it works on my machine'.

plain: Activate the virtual environment in your current shell so python and pip point at it.
when: Right after creating a venv. On Windows PowerShell use .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 instead.

plain: Install every package listed in requirements.txt at the pinned versions.
when: You cloned a Python project and need its dependencies before running it.

flags.meaning: read the package list from a file

plain: Write the exact versions of every installed package to requirements.txt.
when: Before sharing a project, so other people can install the same versions.

plain: Run a Python script with the interpreter currently active in your shell.
when: You want to start your program. If a venv is active, its Python is used.

plain: Serve the current folder over HTTP at http://localhost:8000 — a one-line static web server.
when: You need a local server for HTML, or want to share files on your LAN for testing.

plain: Pretty-print and validate a JSON file, or reformat it with indentation.
when: A JSON file is one long line, or you need to check whether it's valid.

plain: Run the test suite quietly, printing only failures and a summary.
when: You're iterating on code and want fast feedback without a wall of dots.

flags.meaning: only run tests matching an expression
rerun only the tests that failed last time

plain: Print the Python version that would run your code.
when: A tutorial says 'requires Python 3.10+' and you need to check.
